recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future requirement for stronger narrative completeness or explicit negative/wildtype genomic-result guidance should be raised as a new current-scope issue against the Genomics Reporting IG or current Observation/DiagnosticReport genomic guidance, not by restoring obsolete Observation genetics profile wording.
issue_request: FHIR-7236 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Clinical Genomics change request against an old Observation genetics example whose narrative omitted clinically essential structured variant-result information; the resolution said to add guidance about semantic equivalency, the Clinical Sequencing Domain Analysis Model, and then-current limitations around clinically relevant negative or wildtype results.
initial_application: The request was historically applied in commit 45025abf6c99388591b956ef20357479b9a0e7ab, which added the distinctive resolution sentences to source/observation/observation-genetics-introduction.xml for the old Observation genetics profile.
additional_context: The old Observation genetics profile and obs-genetics-example1-somatic artifact targeted by the issue are no longer active current-build content. Commit 3cfe12f1b4037e4fe922af288ba96fa49faf1435 removed outdated clinical genomics artifacts under Observation, DiagnosticReport, and ServiceRequest and streamlined genomics.html. Current active notes for Observation and DiagnosticReport now describe genomic reporting as structured, computable data using those resources and link to the Genomics Reporting IG; the Diagnostics hierarchy includes genomics.html, and fhir.ini keeps Observation active. Zulip and Confluence searches found no community evidence that conflicts with this interpretation.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding the old DSTU1 profile-specific caveat to current source would be redundant and partly stale because the current source has replaced those artifacts with broader current-scope genomic reporting guidance.
